body:
N-34 SLICE 1, CLEAN-UP AFTER P2-25 (helper-n34f, 17 Nov 2026; branch task/N-34-slice1-cleanup-after-p225; server + docs only; BUILT, NOT WALKED; N-34 stays todo, NOT marked built; slice 2 NOT started; no request, no device, no VM 108).
1. ERA-0 GUARDS OUT. Removed: the hit-side skip_rule (HitReason loses it) and the survives_fold_whole call on the album artist, plus every false sentence (album_finder docstring and comments, the N-34 section and the P2-25 sentences about N-34's guards in docs/tasks/P2-songs-as-references.md, the CHANGELOG line). PROOF they decided nothing: differential run of OLD (main) against NEW over 6,000 generated songs/hit lists (Latin, accents, Arabic, Cyrillic, CJK, no-letter names, noise words): 0 decisions differ (refusal, accepted hits 875 = 875, wanted_albums, outcome); only the LABEL of 2,833 refused hits changes (skip_rule -> artist or title_or_version); 448 (song artist, album artist) pairs: 0 differences; every single character of planes 0 and 1 (60,226 fail the rule): not survives_fold_whole implies empty norm_artist and norm_title (now a test). STILL REACHABLE, kept: step 0 refuses a name with no letter or digit and a name the word rules empty (VEVO, Audio) and still ASKS survives_fold_whole (the one definition; a stub test pins the call). The same implication means that call is subsumed today: stated in the code and in the test. Rows under era 1 (two Arabic songs + ONE hit; Habibi + two Arabic words; Fairuz Habibi + either Arabic suffix vs the Latin hit; no-letter name in any alphabet) mutation-checked.
2. FIXTURE NAMES. New encore_server/fixture_names.py (stdlib only) = the ONE function; album_dryrun, tools/record_catalogue_fixtures.py and tests/catalogue_fakes import it (identity tests, no copy). A search is named search_track_<latin prefix <= 40>_<sha256(full query)[:16]>. Red test first: the second Arabic query was answered with the first one's file. Nothing re-recorded, no request: the 2 step-0 search recordings git-mv renamed, the other 8 are named by id and unchanged; a test resolves all 10 ledger entries. A --live dry run over a non-Latin library is now trustworthy.
3. _id_order: isascii() before isdigit() (superscript digits raised ValueError; red test via the matcher).
4. Timing test: injected clock, asserts the pauses the gate asks for (replay: none; 3 live requests: two gaps of 0.25 s), not seconds.
5. record_type counts: the old 49/1/13 added two lists (Bob Marley's and LANDMVRKS'). True: 228 distinct releases in all tracked real recordings (8 server answers + the 20 searches of app/test/fixtures/deezer/search.json): album 114, single 104, ep 10. NO compile and NO live/remix value was ever recorded. A test pins it.
6. INTERACTIVE DEFAULT made TRUE: Catalogue.album gave a person route's song-list request wait_s = what was left of 2.5 s (none before) and its follower 2x that. Now each request keeps the whole deadline (route: exactly as before slice 1); only the CALLER's wait is what is left. Visible difference: none. Exact tests with a 0.4 s first answer.
7. docs/18 (and the keyrepair docstring): Layer 2 = exists, not empty, SQLite header; NOT an integrity check. CHANGELOG N-34 line re-read.
MUTATIONS: 31 of the changed code in a throwaway copy, all killed. Two survivors were handled, not ignored: the empty-album-artist clause was equivalent (dead; removed) and the recorder's isascii test was shadowed by the naming function (a test now asserts the message).
GATES: whole server suite on 3.12, ruff check/format, mypy, check_rows, check_order (see the PR).
FOR THE LEAD: (a) the best-of ruling (a, b, c) is STILL owed before slice 2 stores a stamp; (b) slice-2 scope of the 17 Nov note is written into the design table, not built; (c) PR #110's Arabic rows now hold by key equality, as the note asked; (d) my hash names mean a --answers folder saved by an older run (none exists) would not be found: that is the safe direction.
